# Integration fixtures

What the command-line tools holzWave wraps (`kubectl`, `az`, GAM, `talosctl`) print, as sanitised files that the parser
tests read. Every file below this directory, except this one, is listed in the table exactly once with its source:

- `recorded`: a real run of the tool produced it, through `scripts/record-integration-fixtures.sh`. The run used scratch
  configuration only, a closed environment and read verbs only, and the output passed
  `scripts/sanitise-integration-fixture.py` (identifiers, names and addresses are synthetic).
- `written`: the tool could not be run here (it is absent, or no account is signed in), so the file was written by hand
  from the tool's documents. Replace it with a real capture on a machine that has the tool; no parser has to change.
- drift: a variant of a fixture with a changed shape (an unknown member, a missing member, a wrong type, a cut in the
  middle of a value). It is always `written`, its note starts with `drift`, and its base fixture sits next to it.

Re-record with `sh scripts/record-integration-fixtures.sh <tool|all>`, review `git diff` for anything real, then run
`cargo test -p holzwave-core --test integrate_real`. The tests refuse a fixture that is missing from this table, is listed
twice or is listed and absent, a `recorded` row without a tool version, and a fixture that holds a secret or an identity.

The real-tool tests in the same file run with `HW_INTEGRATION_REAL=1`.

| File | Source | Tool and version | Date | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `kubectl/config_view_canary.kubeconfig` | written | kubectl 1.36.1 reads it | 2026-10-18 | scratch kubeconfig with canary secrets: a bearer token and an exec plugin whose environment holds a value; the one file that may hold them |
| `kubectl/config_view.json` | recorded | kubectl 1.36.1 | 2026-10-18 | `config view -o json` of the canary kubeconfig; the tool redacts the token itself; it does not redact exec environment values, so the recorder replaces them with `REDACTED` |
| `kubectl/version_client.json` | recorded | kubectl 1.36.1 | 2026-10-18 | `version --client -o json`; a version, a build date and a platform, no identity; the sanitiser kept the commit |
| `kubectl/namespaces.json` | recorded | kubectl 1.36.1 | 2026-10-18 | `get namespaces -o json` against a local fake API server (three namespaces); the envelope (`kind: List`, keys sorted) is the real tool's, the items are synthetic |
| `kubectl/pods.json` | recorded | kubectl 1.36.1 | 2026-10-18 | `get pods -n default -o json` against the same fake API server: one running pod with two ready containers, one pending, one in back-off with restarts; the items are synthetic |
| `kubectl/pods_hostile.json` | written | kubectl 1.36.1 shape | 2026-10-18 | input of the hostile-output tests: a 253-character name, terminal escapes, a right-to-left override, a zero-width space, a line break and a 5000-character value written as JSON escapes, an unknown member at every level, a string where a number belongs; generated by a short script, all escapes ASCII |
| `az/version.json` | recorded | az 2.90.0 | 2026-10-18 | `az version -o json` in an empty configuration directory (so no extensions); first run in a fresh directory about 2.1 s, second about 0.1 s |
| `az/account_show_signed_out.stderr.txt` | recorded | az 2.90.0 | 2026-10-18 | standard error of `az account show -o json` in an empty configuration directory: exit status 1, empty standard output |
| `az/account_list.json` | recorded | az 2.90.0 | 2026-10-18 | `az account list -o json` read from a copy of a signed-in profile (no token file) in a scratch directory; the strict sanitiser kept only the structure: ids are synthetic, names are `Item N`, the address is `user@example.com` |
| `az/account_show.json` | recorded | az 2.90.0 | 2026-10-18 | `az account show -o json` from the same copy, same sanitiser; it has `environmentName` where the list has `cloudName` |
| `az/group_list.json` | written | az 2.90.0 shape | 2026-10-18 | `az group list -o json` needs a token and the network and carries names the sanitiser cannot know; written from the documented members (`id`, `location`, `managedBy`, `name`, `properties.provisioningState`, `tags`, `type`) with a provisioning state of `Deleting` and `tags` of `null` as edge cases; replace by a real capture (owner row) |
| `gam/version.txt` | recorded | GAM 7.46.02 | 2026-10-18 | `gam version` in an empty `GAMCFGDIR` (first run: it prints the `Created:` and `Initialized` lines); the clock line is fixed, the install path is `/home/user/...`, the project address is replaced by the sanitiser; first run about 0.25 s |
| `gam/showsections.txt` | recorded | GAM 7.46.02 | 2026-10-18 | `gam showsections` in an empty directory: a `Config File:` header line, then `  DEFAULT *` (two spaces, the name, the mark of the selected section) |
| `gam/print_users.csv` | written | GAM 7.46.02 documents | 2026-10-18 | `print users` needs a signed-in domain: five rows with a multi-line cell holding a comma and doubled quotes, a blank cell and a suspended user; replace by a real capture (owner row) |
| `gam/info_domain.json` | written | GAM 7.46.02 documents | 2026-10-18 | `info domain formatjson` needs a signed-in domain: the members `customerDomain`, `creationTime`, `isVerified` and two `domainAliases` are an assumption from the documents; replace by a real capture (owner row) |
